Hjelm et al. (2019); Tschannen et al. (2020) show that representation learning can be seen as maximizing
mutual information between inputs and their latent representations. Zhai et al. (2024a); Wang et al. (2024a);
Saunshi et al. (2022); Wang et al. (2022); Lee et al. (2021); Brady et al. (2023, 2025) study how learned
representations transfer across tasks and distributions. The works on feature dynamics (Wang and Isola,
2020; Wang et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2025; Wen and Li, 2021) and equivariance/invariance (Gupta et al.,
2024; Garrido et al., 2023c; Xiao et al., 2021) focus on how representations evolve during training and how
structural constraints, such as symmetry or transformation consistency, shape the learned embedding space.
